claim: In the ideal Glover–Balmer stream-depletion model, a constant-rate pumping pulse of duration \(\tau>0\) has a unique global maximum normalized stream-depletion rate at time \(t_*\) after pumping begins, with \(t_* > \max\{\tau,2a/3\}\), \(t_* < \tau+2a/3\), where \(a=d^2S/(4T)\); moreover \(dt_*/d\tau\in(0,1)\), so the peak time rises less than one-for-one with pulse duration.
integrity: The proof is analytic under the stated model. No independent audit or independent validation is claimed.
scientific_limitations: Ideal homogeneous, isotropic, laterally unbounded confined aquifer; constant transmissivity and storage; straight fully penetrating fixed-stage stream.
One constant-rate rectangular pumping pulse only; linear superposition is assumed.
The peak time is specified implicitly rather than in elementary closed form.
Full text of the 1968 intermittent-pumping report and the 2014 review was not available in the consulted route; residual prior-work risk remains.
title: Peak timing after a finite pumping pulse in the Glover–Balmer stream-depletion model
